Subject: Request: provisional quota bump for WarmStart week (Nov 1-7)

Hi Priya —

Quick note from the launch ops side: Tilbury is planning a promotional test the first week of November that will spike traffic for product recommendation calls. We ran an internal dry-run and expect a 6x increase in request volume for 72 hours, with tails into the next week.

Can Redwood provision a provisional quota uplift for Nov 1–7 so we don’t hit rate limits during the promo window? We expect ~40k calls/day at peak (vs 7k steady today). If you need specifics I attached our expected traffic CSV.

Key asks:
- Provisional transient quota increase (burst window authorization)
- A documented fallback routing if the main model reaches soft-limit
- Clear point of contact for runtime alerts during the window

Thanks — appreciate your help.

Emily Torres
Launch Ops Manager, Tilbury Retail
emily.torres@tilburyretail.com

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: provisional quota bump for WarmStart week (Nov 1-7)

Priya / team — reviewed the CSV quickly. TL;DR: we can offer a staged transient uplift if Tilbury agrees to a 4-stage fallback plan. Details: 

1) Proposal: temporary reserved token band of 1.2M tokens/day for Nov 1–7 (covers 45k calls/day assuming 27 tokens/call median).
2) Fallbacks (ordered):
   a) Route to a quantized-compatible variant (Q2) with 30% cost and 10–15% quality delta
   b) If Q2 saturated, route lower-priority calls to cached-prefix responses for identical product queries
   c) If still constrained, apply progressive throttling by user cohort (guest -> anonymous first)
3) Monitoring hooks: per-token latency SLO alarms at 95th p95 / 99th p99 thresholds; auto-notify Ops channel and AM.

Open questions:
- Do we need to reserve burst capacity in a specific region (Tilbury runs US-WEST primarily)? If yes we'll need to mark capacity in us-west-prod.
- If customer wants a hard guarantee (SLA), legal will need to sign a short-term amendment.

I'll sync with Ops on capacity carve-outs but wanted to get the product constraints on the record.

Marcus Lin
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 12:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: provisional quota bump for WarmStart week (Nov 1-7)

+1 on Marcus' staged plan. From an Ops/runbook perspective:

- We can carve a soft-burst pool in us-west (NVidia A100 pool) for Nov 1–7, but it needs a commit horizon (we need headcount on the infra side for pre-warm and a 72-hour lookahead by capacity team).
- Recommended runbook:
   * T-72h: pre-warm token caches + warm persistent KV for prefix caching
   * During window: continuous pacing with 10s aggregation windows, dynamic batching tweak to 48ms target latency
   * Escalation: Pager Duty sequence -> Ops Lead (Connor) -> Product (Marcus) -> AM (Priya)

Operational constraints / asks for the customer:
- Confirm region (confirm us-west) and peak hour estimate (we need hour-by-hour peak if >20k/min).
- Approve routing to quantized variant as primary fallback (Tilbury needs to accept potential quality delta).

Attachment: warmstart_quota_sheet.xlsx (contains proposed carve allocations).

Connor O'Brien
Senior Infra Operations, Redwood Inference
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Thanks all — short security/controls check:

- Transient quota increases do not change our retention posture, but will increase audit-log volume. We should confirm log retention for the event window (ops suggested keeping detailed logs for +30 days). If Tilbury requires longer retention we need to scope storage costs.
- Data residency: Tilbury's traffic is routed through us-west only, so no cross-region copies expected.
- Approvals: For a non-contracted uplift (ad-hoc), Finance needs AM sign-off that the uplift will be billed as a surge add-on. Karthik, can you confirm the billing model and whether we need a temporary PO?

Action items summary (for Priya to relay to Tilbury):
1) Customer confirm region = us-west and provide hourly peak estimate if >20k/min.
2) Customer accept fallback to quantized model Q2 (we'll provide a short quality note).
3) Customer agree to 30-day log retention minimum for the window (or sign a short storage addendum).
4) AM / Sales to confirm billing approach (surge add-on vs short amendment).

I'll stand by for any compliance exceptions if Tilbury asks for longer retention.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
